commentary: Market breadth at 59.9% reflects a split market where energy and broad commodities are surging under persistent inflation pressures, while fixed income assets and non-yielding metals break down under elevated rate hike expectations. The portfolio is positioned to align risk sleeve exposure with this commodity and selective tech momentum while exiting assets whose technical structure has failed. We refuse to overweight the bond sleeve beyond a baseline 0.30 target because long and intermediate Treasury yields continue to reach multi-year highs, rendering fixed duration unhelpful as a hedge right now. A drop in commodity benchmarks below their 200-day moving averages alongside Treasury bond funds reclaiming their 200-day averages would trigger a re-evaluation back toward fixed income duration.
allocation_reason: The 0.30 target sits 0.05 above the 0.25 minimum and 0.45 below the 0.75 maximum. surgering yields leave Treasury funds trading below their 200-day averages, making bonds an ineffective hedge; maintaining a 0.30 sleeve preserves essential ballast without over-allocating to declining fixed income assets.
